dialectic_sweep: An outer or nested cross-store lock was rejected because neither materializer exports a retained-lease contract and the new lock cannot supply global filesystem atomicity.
Rollback or deletion was rejected because a valid content-addressed source remains owned by its completed source transaction when later work fails.
A persistent composition descriptor was rejected because no consumer requires it yet and it would add an unneeded publication, migration, and reproof surface.
Independent WSP_00/WSP_97 review found the publication-field type confusion; a second local audit found and closed the same class on reuse observations.
first_principles: Sequential reproof establishes only that the durable source identity remained equal around one dependency transaction and the two tree identities match.
Equal content identities do not authenticate an upstream producer, seal imports or child effects, or prove simultaneous-store observation.
